# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2, Nov 2026)

## Constraints we're working within
- **People:** Morgan works evenings and weekends. Priya Raman has offered about 5 hrs/week of data-analysis help.
- **Money:** Up to $2,000 of Morgan's savings this year. Outside funding may follow, for example Emberfall rapid grants ($5–25k, closing 30 Nov).
- **Public identity:** Morgan's name stays off all public material (posts, letters, press, public comments, the website) until Morgan has talked to Dorrance HR. Section 7 of the employment agreement covers this, and the outside-activities disclosure is due 30 Nov. **This conversation should happen first. It unblocks everything public.**

## Where a tiny project can actually add value
Big labs and well-funded organisations already cover frontier research, policy advocacy and general commentary. A one-to-two-person, part-time project does best on narrow, careful, cheap work that others can reuse:

1. **Public tracking of safety incidents and commitments (recommended core project).**
   There's a proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042). If it passes, someone has to check whether reporting actually happens. Even if it doesn't pass, nobody keeps an organised, sourced, structured dataset of:
   - publicly reported AI safety incidents (what happened, which model or lab, when disclosed, how quickly), and
   - published lab safety commitments, and whether each one has verifiably been met.
   It fits our skills (Python and data analysis, plus careful writing), costs little, compounds over time, and helps journalists, researchers and regulators. It's also politically neutral and evidence-first, which protects credibility.
2. **A small reading or working group.** It costs nothing, helps recruit volunteers like Priya, and keeps the work honest.
3. **Later: re-granting or connecting people.** Only once there's a track record.

We're deliberately *not* doing: another newsletter, hot takes, or signing advocacy letters before the HR question is settled and Morgan has decided which positions the org takes.

## 90-day plan
| When | What |
|---|---|
| This week | Morgan talks to HR. Decide whether to renew the domain ($14.99). Reply to Priya. |
| By 30 Nov | Submit the Emberfall proposal (draft in `grants/emberfall-rapid-2026.md`). File the Dorrance disclosure. |
| Dec | Build the tracker schema and seed it with ~50 sourced incidents and ~30 commitments. Priya leads data QA. |
| Jan | Publish v0 of the dataset and site (`site/`) once public identity is cleared. Invite corrections. |
| Feb | First short analysis write-up. Possibly submit it to Alignment Commons. |

## Spending (out of the $2,000)
- Domain: $14.99/yr. Recommended, because it keeps the org email address working.
- Pagewell Pro ($240/yr): **not needed yet.** The free subdomain is enough until we launch.
- Everything else is free tooling for now.

# DRAFT: Emberfall Fund rapid grant proposal
*Not submitted. Morgan must review, edit and submit it personally: the named applicant has to be the accountable person and will sign the grant agreement. Deadline: 30 Nov 2026. Also check that taking a grant doesn't conflict with Dorrance section 7 (paid outside work).*

## Project title
Frontier AI Incident & Commitment Tracker

## What we'll do
We'll build and maintain an open, sourced dataset of (a) publicly reported safety incidents involving frontier AI systems and (b) public safety commitments made by frontier developers, with each commitment's verifiable status. Every entry will include its primary sources, its dates (event, disclosure, response) and a confidence rating. Alongside the data we'll publish a short methods note and a quarterly analysis covering things like time-to-disclosure, which commitments were met, missed or are unverifiable, and recurring incident types.

**Why now:** the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042) would require 72-hour reporting. An independent baseline dataset makes it possible to judge whether such rules work, and fills the gap if they don't pass.

## Why us
Morgan Hale writes clearly and programs in Python, and has committed evenings and weekends. Priya Raman, a data analyst, has volunteered ~5 hrs/week for data quality. We're independent, with no lab affiliation and no advocacy position. *[Morgan: add 2–3 lines on your background.]*

## Deliverables (6 months)
1. Month 2: public dataset v0 (≥75 incidents, ≥40 commitments) under CC-BY, plus the methods note.
2. Month 4: corrections process and a simple website.
3. Month 6: analysis report and dataset v1.

## Budget (request: $9,500)
| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Part-time research assistance / contractor for source verification (~120 hrs × $50) | $6,000 |
| Stipend for volunteer data QA | $1,500 |
| Hosting, domain, tools (12 months) | $500 |
| External methods review by a domain expert | $1,000 |
| Contingency | $500 |
| **Total** | **$9,500** |

# DRAFT: Public comment on FMIR-2026-0042 (Frontier Model Incident Reporting)
*Not filed. Comments are published with the filer's name and organisation, so filing waits for Morgan's HR conversation. Deadline: 20 Nov 2026. Morgan should edit it to reflect their own views before filing.*

---

I support the proposed requirement that frontier developers report serious safety incidents within 72 hours, and I offer four suggestions to make it work better:

1. **Define "serious incident" with concrete examples.** Without them, developers will read the term narrowly. Include examples such as: unexpected dangerous capabilities found after deployment; safeguard bypasses that are actively exploited; model-weight theft or leakage; and significant autonomous actions outside intended scope.
2. **Publish anonymised aggregate statistics.** Confidential reports should feed a regular public summary (counts by category, median time to report) so the public and researchers can judge whether the regime is working.
3. **Protect whistleblowers.** Employees who report incidents the developer failed to report should be explicitly protected.
4. **Review the rule after it starts.** Commit to reviewing the definitions and thresholds 18 months after the rule takes effect, using the data collected.

Independent tracking of publicly known incidents suggests many are disclosed late or only through third parties. A clear, enforceable reporting duty would close that gap.

*[Name / organisation: to be filled in by Morgan]*

Halcyon Threshold

An independent, volunteer-run project working toward a good outcome from the arrival of superintelligent AI.

What we're building

The Frontier AI Incident & Commitment Tracker: an open, sourced dataset of publicly reported AI safety incidents and of the safety commitments frontier developers have made, along with whether each commitment has been kept.

Evidence first, no hot takes. Corrections welcome.

Coming early 2027.

# Incident & Commitment Tracker: schema v0

## incidents.csv
| field | description |
|---|---|
| id | INC-0001… |
| title | short description |
| developer | organisation responsible for the model |
| model | model name/version if known |
| category | capability_surprise / safeguard_bypass / misuse / security_leak / autonomy / other |
| event_date | when it happened (best estimate) |
| disclosure_date | first public disclosure |
| disclosed_by | developer / researcher / journalist / user / regulator |
| severity | 1–4 per methods note |
| sources | semicolon-separated URLs (primary sources preferred) |
| confidence | high / medium / low |
| notes | |

## commitments.csv
| field | description |
|---|---|
| id | COM-0001… |
| developer | |
| commitment | verbatim or close paraphrase |
| date_made | |
| source | URL |
| verifiable | yes / partially / no |
| status | met / partly_met / not_met / unclear / pending |
| evidence | URLs supporting the status |
| last_reviewed | date |

## Rules
- Every claim needs a source. Use archived links where possible.
- Two-person review before an entry's status changes to `met` or `not_met`.
- Neutral wording. Record what happened, not judgments about it.

# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

- `strategy.md`: current strategy and 90-day plan
- `tracker/`: Frontier AI Incident & Commitment Tracker (core project)
- `grants/`: funding proposals (drafts)
- `drafts/`: public-facing material waiting on Morgan's review
- `site/`: website (not yet published)
- `old/`: abandoned earlier work, kept for reference only

3. Later, some simple analysis, e.g. time-to-disclosure.

Thanks again,
Morgan
